setting: Three adults sharing a rented flat in an inner-city neighbourhood of a UK city.
background: Hayley, Junior and Yousif share a rented three-bed flat in an inner-city neighbourhood and have lived together for a while. They get on fine without being close friends: Hayley is the sociable one, Junior chats to everyone, Yousif mostly keeps to his room. It is a Friday evening in mid-November, dark since about 16:15 and cold. Hayley and Yousif work from home today, and Junior is off until his 07:00 Saturday shift.
common_knowledge: They have shared the flat for a good while and know each other's routines, but they are flatmates rather than close friends.
Rent is split three ways and paid by standing order to the letting agent on the 1st. Energy, broadband and council tax are split equally.
Heating is on a timer (morning and evening) and everyone is wary of the gas bill, so the thermostat stays low.
Food is bought separately. Staples like tea, milk and washing-up liquid are loosely shared and whoever runs out tells the others.
Bins go out Sunday night for Monday morning collection. Recycling and general waste alternate weekly.
Junior works 07:00-19:00 on Sat and Sun, so the flat is quiet in the morning and he is tired that evening.
Hayley uses the kitchen table for work Thursday and Friday, so others avoid it in office hours.
The nearest shop is a Tesco Express and a corner shop that stays open late. The local pub runs a quiz on Thursdays.
The bathroom has an extractor that barely works, and there is damp in the corner of Hayley's room which she has reported to the agent.

people.profile: Hayley is 41, a marketing associate at a mid-sized company with an office in the city centre. She is in the office Monday to Wednesday and works from home Thursday and Friday, usually at the kitchen table or on her bed with a laptop. She rents a three-bed flat with two flatmates in an inner-city neighbourhood. She is single and fairly happy about it, though her mum keeps asking. Sociable and warm, she is the one who suggests a takeaway night or checks whether anyone wants a tea. She is reasonably organised but leaves things to the last minute sometimes. She has mild asthma, so cold air and damp bother her a bit, and she carries a blue inhaler. She likes Saturday parkrun-ish jogs when she can face them, pub quizzes, Strictly, baking, and meeting friends. Small concerns right now are the heating bill, a Christmas present list she hasn't started, and getting a Friday-afternoon report sent before she logs off.
people.speech: Chatty, friendly and quick, with lots of "oh my god", "go on then", "you alright?" and "honestly". Laughs easily, asks people questions back, fills silences. Mild, unmarked English accent, a bit of northern-ish casualness. Mildly swears when tired or annoyed. Talks in full, rambly sentences when relaxed.
people.texting: Quick replies, usually within minutes. Medium-length messages, mostly lowercase with relaxed punctuation, a few exclamation marks and the occasional emoji (laughing face, wine glass, heart). Sends several short messages in a row rather than one long one.

people.profile: Junior Edwards is 55, a hospital porter on three 12-hour shifts a week, and this week he works Saturday and Sunday days (07:00-19:00). He is divorced and rents a three-bed flat in an inner-city area, sharing with two other adults. He is chatty, curious and easily enthused, and he picks up new interests quickly. He is also disorganised: bills, washing-up and appointments slip, and he often runs late. He gets wound up or low fast when things go wrong, then bounces back. He likes music (old reggae and soul, plus whatever he's just discovered), football on the radio, cooking big pots of food and talking to anyone on the ward. His health is fair, with a bad knee and some back ache from the job. Money is tight on about 25k. Right now he is thinking about the weekend shifts and what to eat tonight.
people.speech: Warm, loud-ish, quick and tangent-prone. He tells stories, laughs at himself and uses "man", "listen" and "you know what I mean". He speaks in a London-ish, British Caribbean-tinged way, but not heavily. He gets flustered when stressed and talks faster.
people.texting: Short, fast and a bit messy. He uses lowercase, odd punctuation and typos he doesn't fix. He uses the occasional emoji (laughing face, thumbs up). He replies quickly when he's on his phone, but sometimes forgets to reply at all.

contacts.name: Gloria

people.memory: It's Friday, my day off, and it's already going dark. I've got Saturday and Sunday on, 7 till 7, and my knee's grumbling about it. I need to sort something to eat tonight and I still haven't dealt with that gas bill letter. Maybe I'll cook a big pot so the flat can share.

people.name: Yousif Al-Ani
people.temperament: openness average, conscientiousness average, extraversion low, agreeableness low, emotional stability low
people.profile: Yousif is 26, born in Yemen, and has lived in the UK for five years. He came to study and now works as a freelance designer from his bedroom desk, about 30 hours a week, mostly branding and social graphics for small businesses. Money is tight at about 15.8k a year, and invoices that get paid late bother him. He is quiet and reserved, a bit guarded and quick to feel irritated or anxious, and he doesn't go out of his way to be agreeable. He shares a three-bed rented flat with two other adults and mostly keeps to himself. He is single and fine with that, though he sometimes feels flat. He likes sketching, podcasts about design and football, cheap ramen, and long walks when the light lasts. Lately he has been worrying about the heating bill, a client who is slow to pay, and the early dark.
people.speech: Quiet, fairly short sentences, dry and a little clipped. Speaks at an even pace and can sound curt or sarcastic when tired or stressed. Doesn't volunteer much, and answers questions briefly. British-international English with a slight accent. Says "yeah", "fine", "whatever" and "to be honest". Avoids small talk but will complain about practical things like dishes or bills.
people.texting: Short, lowercase, minimal punctuation, no emoji. Replies can be slow, sometimes hours, and are often one line. Uses "ok" and "yeah". Longer only when annoyed or when it is about work.
